summary: Arvin stands inside the hollowed-out hull of a rusted fuel tanker, his hands trembling as he holds a tattered blueprint against the corrugated wall. Milo sits on a crate of salvaged brass, aggressively shoving a corroded industrial spring into a jagged fuel valve with his grease-stained thumbs. The sunlight cuts through the ceiling in sharp, golden slats, illuminating the swirling dust and the tactile grime on Milo’s goggles. Arvin watches the valve seat, his eyes tracking the uneven metal edges as they threaten to snap under the forced tension of the makeshift assembly. "This bypass will hold exactly three seconds after ignition, so don't blink."
settingText: The interior of the nomadic rusted tanker workshop.

dialogueInline.text: This weld won't hold five atmospheres, Milo.
I can feel the seal seating without the gauge.
This isn't a payload, it's a kill-switch.
Keep your weight low or the wind takes us.

SUBTEXT — The pressure of failure is becoming a physical weight that Arvin can no longer hide from his apprentice.
CAMERA / PERFORMANCE — Focus on the micro-expression of doubt in Arvin's eyes as the lamp flickers.
CONTINUITY — The cracked oxygen canister nozzle.

summary: In the shadow of a tilting solar array, Arvin watches Lucia as she slides a heavy, unlabeled lead container across the dry, cracked earth. Lucia keeps her gaze fixed on the horizon, her fingers tracing the sharp, cold edge of the crate while Arvin remains motionless with his arms crossed tightly over his chest. The heat haze ripples between them, distorting the scorched landscape as Arvin steps forward to block her path to the primary mixing station. He points toward the corporate insignia scratched off the side of the crate with a jagged piece of flint. "Your refusal to see this as a weapon makes you a liability to the people you claim to save."
settingText: Arvin and Milo in the nomadic launch-shop.

dialogueInline.text: This seam will liquefy at four thousand feet if we don't reinforce the structural jacket with the high-carbon scrap.
The physics don't care where the steel came from, Arvin, they only care that the tension holds the seal for sixty seconds.
I found a way to bridge the ignition gap, but you're not going to like how much heat this mixture generates on ascent.
The thermal signature from their welding torch is a beacon; move the interceptor team to the canyon mouth immediately.

summary: Cyrus stands on a high limestone ridge, peering through long-range optics that capture Arvin in the valley below, who is currently hauling a heavy tarp over a cache of metal drums. The heat haze ripples between them, making Arvin’s movements appear jagged as he wipes sweat from his forehead and looks toward the horizon. Cyrus remains perfectly still, his gloved hand resting on the holstered grip of his sidearm while he tracks the path through the dunes. The sunlight glints off the lens of the optics, casting a sharp flare across Cyrus’s stoic face. "They are leaving a trail of industrial garbage that leads straight to their grave."
settingText: The interior of the Nomad Tanker.

dialogueInline.text: This alloy won't hold past Mach three without a secondary thermal wrap.
Precision is a luxury we traded for oxygen three weeks ago, Arvin.
This chip could turn your toy into a needle that pops the Aegis bubble.
Deploy the kinetic harpoons once the heat signature reaches ignition threshold.
